mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the trigger fires but returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate near historical lows, signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressures and input costs, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth offsets cost pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the trigger is met but returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average, coupled with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), indicates a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average for four consecutive months and GDPC1 < 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in more than 35% of cases.
